newsitem.title: USA: New World says franchise program cuts costs.
newsitem.headline: New World says franchise program cuts costs.

text.p: New World Coffee Inc said it expects to cut corporate general and administrative expenses by about 20 percent, or $150,000 per quarter, by shifting to a franchise system.
The company said this change will be visible in the second and third quarter financial results and will help accelerate its profitability.
The company said it expects to add 30 franchises through the remainder of 1997.
Each store would generate a franchise fee of $25,000 plus an ongoing cash flow stream of about 10 percent of franchisee revenues. Target store revenues are $700,000 annually.
The company said these franchisee revenues would be generated through a combination of royalties, marketing contributions and proprietary product sales.
New World said franchised stores require significantly less capital than the $300,000 investment required for company stores.
